name: Core Allocation
description: Codifies SWE core allocation (performance vs efficiency) and model-by-difficulty assignment so TPM dispatches at the right scale and cost.

performanceCores.label: Performance Cores
performanceCores.description: Number of high-capability SWE slots TPM may use concurrently. Performance cores handle the main task — primary code work, complex logic, critical path. Always dispatched first. Raise for parallel-heavy workflows; lower for cost-conscious sessions.

efficiencyCores.label: Efficiency Cores
efficiencyCores.description: Number of lower-priority SWE slots TPM may use concurrently. Efficiency cores handle side tasks when performance cores are busy — minor fixes, research passes, simple changes. Set to 0 to disable secondary parallelism entirely.

modelByDifficulty.label: Model By Difficulty
modelByDifficulty.description: User-managed map of task-difficulty tier to model name. TPM selects the model per dispatch based on the assignment's declared difficulty. Defaults match the SWT convention (Haiku for low, Sonnet for medium, Opus for high). Adjust per project — e.g. drop Opus entirely for cost control, or promote everything to Opus for max quality.

highPriorityMode.label: High Priority Mode
highPriorityMode.description: How TPM dispatches when the user signals a high-priority task. all-hands deploys EVERY available SWE slot (performance + efficiency) on the same task — all-hands-on-deck. perf-only deploys performance cores only; efficiency stays on standby. normal ignores priority hints; dispatches per the standard performance-first pattern. Default all-hands matches the SWT convention.

announceDispatchPlan.label: Announce Dispatch Plan
announceDispatchPlan.description: When on, TPM proactively tells the user its dispatch plan before spawning SWEs (Putting SWE-1 and SWE-2 on the main logic with Opus, SWE-3 on standby for side tasks). When off, TPM dispatches silently. On builds trust and lets the user redirect; off cuts session-output noise.
